correctness.rationale: For all positive trinomial outcome probabilities, the direct monotone-argument proof gives simple strictly interlacing zeros of the two parity generating polynomials. Partial fractions have positive residues. Strict Newton log-concavity for each removed factor yields both strict ratio inequalities and forces every mode pair to be adjacent. Polynomial coefficient limits give weak inequalities at boundary; real-rooted limiting sequences have at most two neighboring modal indices, and both forbidden 5/2-gap tie configurations contradict the weak inequalities. The two-summand boundary witness yields exactly 3/2. Exact-integer code passes 60,986 full-positive cases and 52,686 boundary cases; arbitrary n and real weights follow analytically, not from finite tests.

originality.rationale: The directly inspected March 2026 primary source proves a 5/2 maximum separation for arbitrary pairs of parity-conditioned modes (Theorem 1 and Proposition 3) and does not state or imply the sharp 3/2 boundary or universally adjacent 1/2 interior result without the new joint coefficient-ratio analysis. The inspected 2024 work treats Darroch and cross-modality of Bernoulli sums, not the two parity parts of a trinomial law. Four actual targeted published-finding corpus searches and separate literature searches uncovered no published equivalent statement. Novelty is assessed to best knowledge, with classical Hurwitz total-positivity implication retained as a residual risk.
residual_risks: An older statement formulated for all Hurwitz-stable polynomial even/odd parts, or as total-positivity of their Hurwitz matrices, could imply the coefficient-ratio sandwich; this remains a bibliographic risk rather than a proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The parity-conditional modes of independent three-outcome scoring trials are natural distributional summary statistics. The 2026 motivating source explicitly obtained only 5/2. The proved sharp full-simplex 3/2 and stronger 1/2 interior adjacency, with an attaining boundary example, answer a precise structural gap and distinguish genuine zero-probability degeneracies from generic positive laws.
